name: Ashok Leyland Ltd
title: Ashok Leyland Ltd - 500477 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 record revenue of INR9,634 cr (+10% YoY) but EBITDA flat at INR970 cr and margin down 100bp to 10.1%; inventory buffer masked commodity hit, Q2 guided as peak cost quarter.

summary.headline: Ashok Leyland Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% to INR9,634 crore, a record, but EBITDA was flat at INR970 crore as margin fell 100 bps to 10.1%.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q1 CV volume (48,673 units), revenue (INR9,634 crore, +10% YoY), PAT (INR609 crore, +3%) and cash surplus, while EBITDA margin contracted 100 bps to 10.1% on commodity pressure. Inventory build (about 6,500 to 8,500 vehicles) and cost actions deferred part of the material cost increase, and price hikes offset roughly half of the commodity headwind. Management guided that commodity costs will peak in Q2 FY27 and soften from Q3, with domestic MHCV demand recovering strongly from June. Exports fell 18% on the RAK (UAE) plant disruption, which management expects to recover in the coming quarters.

financial_highlights.change: +90 bps YoY, in line with Q4
Up more than INR1,431 crore YoY

segments.name: Domestic MHCV
segments.commentary: Volume 22,998 units, +15% YoY; market share 29%. Bus volumes fell as the company skipped unprofitable STU tenders; medium bus share rose to about 25% from 15% over 3-4 years.

segments.name: LCV
segments.commentary: Domestic offtake 18,874 units, +21% YoY, highest-ever Q1; VAHAN share 13.2%, up 30 bps YoY.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Volume 2,461 units, -18% YoY, due to RAK plant shutdown in April-May. SAARC and Africa grew 40-60%. RAK output was 600 in June with plans for 700 and 800 in the following months.

segments.name: Non-CV businesses
segments.commentary: Domestic aftermarket revenue +12.7% YoY; Power Solutions revenue +51% YoY; defence revenue +64% YoY.

segments.name: Switch Mobility (EV)
segments.commentary: Won order for 650 e-buses, taking order book to about 2,100; delivered 225 e-buses and close to 300 e-LCVs in the quarter.

segments.name: OHM Mobility (E-MaaS)
segments.commentary: Operational fleet above 1,900 e-buses after adding more than 500 in the quarter; targeting PAT breakeven in the near future.

segments.name: Hinduja Housing Finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR16,157 crore, +13% YoY; PAT INR69 crore, flat YoY; consolidated net NPA 2.1% (book basis, HLF and HHF).

guidance_outlook: Commodity cost pressure expected to peak in Q2 FY27 and be higher than Q1 in impact; softening from Q3 and turnaround in Q4.
Further price increases: MHCV more than 1% and LCV more than 2% taken from July; more being considered before quarter end.

Domestic MHCV industry expected to grow strongly in Q2 (June and July above 20%); management is conservative on the second half, but still expects high single-digit MHCV growth from October onwards, with LCV slightly better.
Capex to keep rising over the next 2-3 years from about INR900-1,000 crore a year; detailed plan to follow.
Manpower cost to rise 4-5% QoQ from the July increment cycle; admin overhead to be tightened through a central cost cell for spends above INR50 lakh.
Breakeven for domestic MHCV volume, after non-MHCV fixed-cost coverage, has fallen to about 1,000-1,500 units a month.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex INR153 crore, focused on new products, future technology, alternate powertrains and EVs; investment in subsidiaries INR10 crore.
RAK (UAE) plant capacity is 600 units, but it was run at 800 with temporary arrangements; output is being restored to 800.
A new Saudi plant is being evaluated for acceleration from its original 18-24 month timeline.
Network touch points at 2,137 (1,177 MHCV, 960 LCV) after adding 33 in Q1, with focus on North and East.
Optare debt of about GBP 50 million remaining; plan to repay GBP 25 million this year and GBP 25 million next year.
demand_pricing: Domestic MHCV industry grew 13% YoY in Q1 (May about 1-2%, June above 20%, July above 20%). Growth drivers: GST recalibration, replacement of BS3/BS4 fleets, financing and infrastructure.
Price increase in Q1 was about 1.2-1.25%; cumulative FY27 price increases are about 2.25% for MHCV and more than 3.5% for LCV.
Commodity costs (steel, natural rubber) remain elevated; price hikes and cost savings offset about half of the Q1 commodity increase each; inventory accounting offset the rest.
Competitive intensity in the MAV segment is rising. The new air-suspension multi-axle truck offers 4 tonnes extra payload, versus 2 tonnes from a competitor product.
Management's BS7 view: not before 2031, possibly 2032.

qa_highlights.question: What was the gross RM headwind in Q1, and how much pricing offset it? What is the pending impact for Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: About four-fifths of Q1 commodity cost increases hit the P&L because one-fifth to one-fourth of requirements came from opening inventory. Price increases and cost savings each offset about 50% of the commodity increase. Remaining inventory-related costs will flow through later, but will be modest.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company investing in HHF when the finance business is being demerged?
qa_highlights.answer: HHF AUM has grown about 34% CAGR over 4 years and net worth about 24%. The investment is growth capital at an arm's-length, independently valued price, and HLF's capital structure cannot be disturbed before the NCLT merger.

qa_highlights.question: What are the mix and truck demand outlook for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: ICV growth has outpaced heavy trucks because of GST-related pricing effects on retail buyers. Fleet and heavy-duty buyers lag, so the mix should improve in Q2 with HIPPO, TAURUS and air-suspension MAV launches.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and export outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex was about INR900-1,000 crore in the last two years and will rise over the next 2-3 years. Exports should recover as RAK ramps to 800 units a month; SAARC and Africa grew 40-60%.

qa_highlights.question: Is competitive intensity rising in the MAV segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says its air-suspension product was a 2.5-3 year engineering project, not a reaction to competitors. It is the first such launch in India, offering 4 tonnes of extra payload.

qa_highlights.question: Can non-MHCV businesses cover fixed costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven domestic MHCV volume has fallen from 6,000-7,000 units a month to about 1,000-1,500 units, as non-MHCV businesses have grown.

risks_watch: Commodity costs: management expects Q2 FY27 to be the peak. Margin recovery depends on Q3 softening and further price increases.
Inventory-led margin benefit is partly timing; the deferred cost will flow into P&L in later quarters.
High base from October 2025 (industry growth of 20-21%) could slow MHCV growth in H2.
RAK/GCC export recovery to 800 units a month, and the new Saudi plant timeline.
Bus market share loss in heavy-duty tenders, as unprofitable orders are declined.
HLF-NDL Ventures reverse merger awaiting NCLT approval.
Regulatory cost burden (mandatory mechanised load covers, AVAS, advanced braking) may need price increases.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and the demand recovery, but cautious on margins; management said Q2 will be the commodity peak and was explicit that Q2 margins will be challenging. The company was candid about the one-off inventory benefit and the export disruption, and conservative on H2 industry growth.
key_quotes: For Q1 FY27, we achieved all-time high CV volume, revenue, profit and cash surplus.
We could use about one fifth to one fourth of the total requirements in this quarter from the opening.
So we are trying to pay another GBP 25 million by this year, and we will pay another GBP 25 million by next year.
Respite from that we think will come in Q3 and Q4 only.

adds.what: New Saudi plant (under evaluation for acceleration from original 18-24 month timeline)
RAK (UAE) plant restoring output to 800 units from 600 rated capacity after April-May shutdown

growth.why: Management guides high single-digit MHCV industry growth from October (conservative H2) and a commodity turnaround in Q4, backed by June/July industry growth above 20%, 1-2% price hikes, RAK output restoration to 800 and a Saudi plant under evaluation, but no firm new capacity timeline or order-book figure for the revenue outlook.
